title: The Splendor That Sank
intro: Picture this: a soul draped in fine garments and surrounded by treasures beyond imagination. This individual believed their wealth was earned through their own brilliance, never acknowledging the source of true provision. Walking among the followers of a mighty prophet, this person refused every call to humility. Today, we uncover the identity of a figure whose magnificent fortune became their final resting place.
clues: I lived during the time of a prophet who called a stubborn nation to truth.
I was part of a chosen community, yet my heart turned away from the message.
Gold and silver captivated me more than any divine command.
My treasure vaults grew so vast that a strong group of men could barely lift the keys.
I boasted that my wealth was given to me because of my own knowledge.
In the end, I and my entire dwelling were swallowed by the earth as a warning.

identity.label: Who Am I?
options: Qarun
Haman
Samiri
Bilqis
Talut (Saul)

trial.label: Trial/Event
options: Arrogance over wealth and refusing charity
Forging a golden idol from melted jewelry
Declaring divinity over a powerful kingdom
Persecuting early believers in Makkah
Leading a campaign to destroy the Sacred House
trial.answer: Arrogance over wealth and refusing charity

location.label: Key Element
options: Treasures whose keys burdened many strong men
A golden calf that produced sound
A glorious throne from a distant land
A trench filled with blazing fire
A mighty army of war elephants
location.answer: Treasures whose keys burdened many strong men

outcome.label: Outcome
options: Swallowed by the earth along with the dwelling
Drowned in the sea with an army
Burned alive in a pit of fire
Destroyed by a howling, raging wind
Struck down by a single mighty blast
outcome.answer: Swallowed by the earth along with the dwelling

arabic: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ فِى زِينَتِهِۦ ۖ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا يَـٰلَيْتَ لَنَا مِثْلَ مَآ أُوتِىَ قَـٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍۢ
verse: So he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qārūn. Indeed, he is one of great fortune." (28:79)
